title: The Food Safety Mitt
description: Five pictures from our own kitchen, one step each. This is not a memory test — every answer is in the picture above it. The point is that the mitt is a food safety tool, not a heat glove, and that one hand stays clean from the cooler to the basket.

questions.title: Pepper has just pulled a Food Safety Mitt out of the box on top of the cooler. What is it actually for?
choices: Protecting her hand from the hot oil
Keeping her hand warm while she is in the cooler
Keeping bare skin off the bag, so nothing from her hand reaches the product
Marking her as the person running the fryer this shift
questions.help: Look at where the mitt is in the picture, and where the fryer is.
questions.explanation:
It is a food safety tool, not a heat glove.

The mitt is thin plastic. It would do nothing against 350°F oil and it never goes near it. Its whole job is to sit between your hand and the bag of raw product, so that whatever is on your hands stays on your hands.

If you have ever thought of it as the fryer glove, that is the thing to unlearn here. Treating it as heat protection is how people end up taking it to the fryer, which is the one place it must never go.

questions.title: The mitt is on. Which hand opens the cooler door?
choices: The bare hand, so the mitted hand stays clean for the bag
The mitted hand, since it is already covered
Either one, as long as she washes up afterwards
Neither — she should use a cloth on the handle
questions.help: One hand is doing a job. The other is being kept out of the way on purpose.
questions.explanation:
The bare hand opens the door. Look at the picture: the mitted hand is held up and clear, touching nothing.

That door handle is one of the dirtiest things in the kitchen — every hand in the building has been on it. The moment the mitt touches it, the mitt is no cleaner than the handle, and it may as well not be there.

This is the step people skip, because opening a door with your awkward hand feels silly. It is the whole reason the mitt works.

questions.title: She is carrying the bag in the mitted hand. Before the bag is empty, what else may that mitted hand touch?
choices: The basket handle
The cooler door, to push it shut behind her
Her apron, to steady the bag
Nothing at all — only the bag
questions.help: Count the things the mitted hand is touching in the picture.
questions.explanation:
Only the bag. Plastic to plastic, cooler to basket, nothing in between.

Once the mitted hand touches anything else — the handle, the door, your apron, your phone — it has picked something up, and the next thing it touches is raw product. The mitt stops being a barrier and becomes a carrier.

If you do touch something, that mitt is finished. Bin it and take a fresh one. They cost pennies.

questions.title: The wings are going into the basket. Where is the basket while that happens?
choices: Over the fryer, so nothing drops on the floor
On a sheet pan on the prep station
In the hand sink
On the shelf inside the cooler
questions.help: The basket is sitting on something in the picture. What is under it?
questions.explanation:
On a sheet pan on the prep station — never over the fryer.

Loading over the oil looks tidier and it is the instinct most people have. But breading, ice and crumbs fall off a frozen portion as it goes in, and every one of them lands in the oil, burns, and darkens the whole vat. You shorten the life of the oil for every basket after yours.

The sheet pan catches all of it and goes in the wash. That is the only reason it is there.

questions.title: Pepper is lowering the basket into the oil. Where is the Food Safety Mitt now?
choices: Still on her hand — it protects her from the oil
In her pocket, ready for the next drop
In the bin with the bag, before she walked to the fryer
Hanging on the rail beside the fryer
questions.explanation:
In the bin, with the bag, before she ever came to the fryer. Both her hands are bare in this picture.

The mitt and the bag are one disposable item. The bag is empty, so the mitt's job is done, and they go in the bin together on the way past.

Keeping it on is the dangerous answer and it is the one people pick, because by now it feels like protective equipment. It is a thin plastic bag. Near 350°F oil it is a hazard to you, not a help.

questions.title: Put the whole thing in order, start to finish.
steps: Take a mitt from the box and put it on one hand
Open the cooler with the bare hand and lift out a portioned bag with the mitted one
Set a basket down on the sheet pan on the prep station
Tip the wings out of the bag into the basket
Bin the empty bag and the mitt together
Carry the basket to the fryer and lower it into the oil
questions.help: There is one step in here that does not appear in the five pictures above.
questions.explanation:
Mitt on, cooler, basket on the pan, tip, bin the bag and mitt, then the fryer.

The step the pictures do not show is binning the bag and the mitt. It happens between the prep station and the fryer, and it is the step that gets dropped when the store is busy — which is exactly how a used mitt ends up back on a door handle or in a pocket.

Notice the shape of it: everything the mitted hand does happens before the fryer. By the time you are standing at the oil, both hands are bare and the only thing you are holding is a basket.
